ADHD Coach

Sound familiar?

The diagnosis came. Then a handout. Then nothing.

  • The appointment is over, the leaflet is on the counter, and the question is still “so what do we actually do at home?”
  • Mornings, homework and bedtime feel like the same fight, every single day.
  • Every planner and 12-step routine works for a week, then quietly disappears.
  • You want a plan that fits real life with an ADHD brain in the house, without turning the whole family upside down.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover live

What’s actually going on

Executive function explained in plain words, so “lazy” and “not trying” finally leave the conversation.

Why “just try harder” never worked

Why willpower runs out, and why systems built for an ADHD brain keep going when motivation doesn’t.

Find your minimum

My Find Your Minimum approach for home: the smallest version of a routine that still counts on the hard days.

Body doubling and other focus tools

Low-effort tools adults use to start and finish the boring stuff, and how to set them up this week.

ADHD kid tips for parents

Fewer words, visual schedules and transition warnings: small changes that make mornings and bedtime calmer.

Meet Emily

Hi, I’m Emily Schwalbach

I was diagnosed with ADHD at 16. I was a kindergarten teacher, then I built my own business, Be Social Consulting, here in Indy, all while raising three boys.

I’m not here as a doctor. I’m here as someone who lives it every day and has spent years figuring out the systems that actually work for an ADHD brain. Now I teach them to ADHD adults and to parents of ADHD kids.

Questions

Before you save your seat

Why is it $17 and not free?

Because people who invest, even a little, show up and actually try what they learn. I want a room full of people ready to try something new.

Is this for adults or for parents?

Both. Most of the class works for anyone living with ADHD, and there’s a dedicated part for parents of ADHD kids.

Is this medical advice?

No. The class is educational content and coaching-style support. It doesn’t replace a doctor, therapist or care team. For anything medical, please speak with your own provider.

What if I can’t make it live?

Save your seat anyway. Every seat includes the full replay.

Will you talk about coaching at the end?

For the last few minutes I’ll share how to apply to work with me, for anyone who wants to go further. Everything before that is yours to use either way.

Script 1 · “The handout”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Here’s what nobody tells families after an ADHD diagnosis.”

Body

“You get the appointment, maybe a handout, and then you’re on your own. I was diagnosed at 16 and spent years figuring out the rest. The first thing to know: it was never about trying harder. It’s about systems that fit how an ADHD brain works.”

CTA

“I’m teaching the whole starter plan live in Welcome to the Team. Seats are $17. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: talking to camera on a plain yellow background (like your profile photo), captions on, end card “Educational content, not medical advice”. No “you have ADHD” language in captions.

Script 2 · “Find your minimum”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Why the 12-step morning routine never lasts in ADHD homes.”

Body

“Big routines work for a week, then disappear. What lasts is the minimum: the smallest version that still counts on the hard days. One step. Then the next. That’s how a routine survives a real Tuesday.”

CTA

“I’ll show you how to find yours, live, for $17, replay included. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: kitchen counter, sticky notes going up one at a time, on-screen text for each step. Reuses your Find Your Minimum idea for the home.

Script 3 · “Three morning tips”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Three ADHD kid tips that make mornings calmer.”

Body

“One: fewer words. Point to the picture instead of repeating the list. Two: a visual schedule at eye level. Three: a five-minute warning before every switch. Small changes, big difference.”

CTA

“There’s a whole parent section in my live class, Welcome to the Team. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: quick cuts with on-screen cards: Fewer words · Visual schedule · Five-minute warning. Your ADHD Kid Tips for Parents style, reused for the class.
